# Independent adversarial review of a finite carrier-to-peer-record experiment

Please act as an independent scientific innovator and adversarial methodologist. Evaluate a
prospective experiment rather than an empirical result. Do not assume that a detailed frozen design
is valid merely because it is detailed, and do not infer support from historical implementation,
tests, prompts, tasks, or closed research directions.

The narrow scientific question is whether, on one finite churned cooperative reservation toy, a
single anonymous shared policy can use an authentic carrier-to-peer-record association to select
the correct one of two capped records and thereby improve native common team return over a matched
within-stratum reassociation of whole valid carriers. One parameterization is trained at roster
envelopes 6 and 8 and evaluated at those envelopes and a held-out envelope 10. Every five-window
episode includes actual leave and rejoin, renewed opaque slot tokens, changing peers and roles,
environment-owned lineage state continuity, one payload read and one reservation service per
subscriber, and common team credit. The publisher's lane reservation is exogenous. Each subscriber
receives a relevant sealed record containing its paired publisher's reservation and a decoy record
containing another active publisher's reservation, opens exactly one, and then chooses a lane.

In the authentic arm, the carrier's hidden semantic bit identifies the physical slot of the
relevant record. In the reassociated arm, whole valid carriers are permuted across other worlds
inside exact roster, occupancy, window, interface, presentation, and balanced-block strata. The
registered donor permutations make the carrier bit conditionally uninformative while preserving
its marginals and validation success. Both arms keep physical worlds, records, slots, work,
resources, roles, churn, learner class, initialization, exogenous random coordinates, update
counts, and evaluation budgets paired. Hidden copy/complement, payload, and lane-action label
polarities are balanced across eight paired seeds. The learner sees only two neutral interface
bits, the carrier surface bit and successful validation before its record choice, and only the
opened payload plus the neutral interface bits before its lane choice. It has no identity, slot
token, lineage, partner, roster size, active-mask position, donor, block, hidden-slot, unopened
payload, pair-score, or future-return feature.

The proposed anonymous learner has shared linear selector and controller heads. All subscribers in
one window act from the same pre-window parameters; after the window, each head receives one
commutative grouped update from the common team mean return, scaled by pair count. Training and
evaluation are paired across arms and seeds. Frozen evaluation includes natural execution, a
masked carrier-bit branch, a forced-relevant-record branch, and a forced-decoy-record branch.
Correct-record selection is the proposed mediator. A positive requires a competent controller on
forced relevant reads, positive authentic-minus-reassociated selection and common-return effects
for every seed at envelopes 6, 8, and 10, material held-out effects, a material forced-relevant
versus forced-decoy return contrast, degradation under masking, and consistent direction across
all hidden polarities, reduced-roster windows, and first-post-rejoin windows. An incomplete support
gate, wrong exact control rates, leakage, unmatched work, failed controller competence, incomplete
paired output, resource breach, or semantic deviation is inconclusive.

The claim ceiling is deliberately finite. Even a positive would establish only acquisition and
held-out-envelope transfer of one carrier-gated deconfliction rule for this exact learner, host,
churn schedule, and common-credit law. It would not establish cryptographic security,
authentication necessity, arbitrary population size, general MARL superiority, continuous flight,
safety, deployment, or superiority over every equally predictive resource-matched feature.

Adversarially decide whether this object truly supports a noncircular causal treatment. In
particular, reconstruct a defensible event order and causal graph: publisher reservation and pair
formation, relevant and decoy record production, record placement, carrier issuance and
validation, reassociation, learner information sets, actions, team reward, and updates. Ask whether
the relevant-record truth exists independently of the carrier bit, whether validation authenticates
a real host event rather than a declared target table, and whether reassociation deletes only the
association while keeping information, work, support, and opportunity matched. Check that both
record choices and both lane choices have real optimal-policy and return headroom; that the
anonymous controller is competent but not a containing explanation for the selector; and that the
forced branches identify correct-record mediation rather than merely correlate with it.

Please also seek a constructive counterexample. The decoy record comes from another active
publisher in a cyclic pairing, while every learner update uses common team return. Could that
cross-pair origin, shared parameters, paired exploration, finite balanced blocks, deterministic tie
ranks, neutral interface bits, or hidden presentations create a treatment-looking selection or
return effect without the claimed association pathway? Conversely, could a same-information
bit-blind or permutation-compatible controller absorb all value? Determine whether actual
leave/rejoin and held-out envelope 10 change a causally relevant exposure or merely decorate an
otherwise independent-window binary cue task. Distinguish a fatal attribution defect from a
meaning-preserving clarification and from a limitation already contained by the finite claim
ceiling.
